classification.difficultyReason: Derives a displacement vector by integration and selects the positive ground-return time.

content.prompt: A particle is projected from ground level at an angle of $45^\circ$ and a speed of $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$ and the point of projection as the origin.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Derive the equation of the displacement vector.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\ddot{x}&=0,\\\ddot{y}&=-10.\end{align*}$$
Using the initial velocity components,
$$\begin{align*}\dot{x}&=15\cos45^\circ\\&=\frac{15\sqrt2}{2},\\\dot{y}&=-10t+15\sin45^\circ\\&=-10t+\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}.\end{align*}$$
Integrating and using $x(0)=y(0)=0$,
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}t,\\y&=-5t^2+\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}t.\end{align*}$$
Therefore
$$\mathbf{s}(t)=\left(\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}t\right)\mathbf{i}+\left(-5t^2+\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}t\right)\mathbf{j}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the time taken to reach the ground.

answer.worked:
At ground level, $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}0&=-5t^2+\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}t\\&=t\left(\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}-5t\right).\end{align*}$$
Thus $t=0$ or $5t=\frac{15\sqrt2}{2}$. The positive time gives
$$t=\frac{3\sqrt2}{2}\text{ s}.$$
